Coram : Siddheshwar S. Thombre, J.
 Date : 5th February, 2026
 P.C.:-
1.
Heard learned Counsel for the respective parties.

2. By way of the present petition, the Petitioner is challenging the order dated 14.03.2019 passed by the Sub-Divisional Officer, Shirdi Division Shirdi/Dy. Collector, Land Acquisition, whereby the application filed by the Petitioner under Section 28-A(3) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, ("the Act" for short) came to be rejected on the ground that the same were not filed within a period of three months.
3.
Mr. Dattatraya Jayabhar, learned Advocate for the Petitioner was not parties to the reference proceedings and, therefore, there was no occasion for them to appear before the Reference Court.
It is submitted that only after the Reference Court passed an award under Section 18 of the Act enhancing the compensation, the Petitioner filed application under Section 28-A(3) of the Act.
Hence, the authority 2 of 3 63-WP.12362.2021 ought not to have rejected the said application on the ground of limitation.

4. Mr. A. D. Wange, learned A.G.P. for Respondent Nos.1 to 3- State authorities opposes the petition by submitting that under Section 28-A of the Act, the limitation prescribed is three months and once a time-bound remedy is provided under the statute, the authority has no power to condone the Maruti Ananda Shinde vs The State Of Maharashtra And Others on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27830687/

sentences.text: Therefore, the Sub-Divisional Officer has rightly rejected the application.
5. Having considered the documents on record and the impugned order, it is evident that the land was acquired by the Petitioner/Claimant by the same notification issued under Section 4 of the Act.
The claimant, being aggrieved by the award passed under Section 11 of the Act, filed a reference under Section 18 of the Act.
After leading evidence, the Reference Court enhanced the compensation.

6. It is an admitted position that the Petitioner was not party to the reference proceedings under Section 18 of the Act and, therefore, naturally, they had no knowledge of the proceedings before the Reference Court.

After coming to know about the enhanced compensation awarded in the reference,
the Petitioner, being similarly situated person whose lands were acquired under the same 3 of 3 63-WP.12362.2021 notification, became entitled to file application under Section 28-A(3) of the Act.

7. In such circumstances, the period of limitation under Section 28-A of the Act cannot be strictly computed from the date of the award of the Reference Court, as the Petitioner was not party to the said proceedings.
The authority, therefore, ought not to have rejected the application solely on the ground of limitation.
In view of the same, I am inclined to allow the petition.
8. The Writ Petition is partly allowed.
The order dated 14.03.2019 passed by the Sub-Divisional Officer, Shirdi Division Shirdi/Dy.
Collector, Land Acquisition is quashed and set aside.
9. The proceedings filed by Petitioner before the Sub-Divisional Officer, Shirdi Division Shirdi/Dy.

Collector, Land Acquisition is restored and it is directed that the S.D.O. shall decide the same in accordance with law.
10. Pending Civil Applications, if any, also stand disposed of.

(SIDDHESHWAR S. THOMBRE, J.) Tauseef Maruti Ananda Shinde vs The State Of Maharashtra And Others on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27830687/
